title: Modern LLM Training Stages
description: The 3-stage LLM pipeline: Pre-training on trillions of tokens, Supervised Fine-Tuning (SFT), and RLHF/DPO preference alignment.

slides.title: The 3-Stage LLM Recipe 🍲
slides.content:
# How Frontier LLMs Are Built

Modern conversational assistants (ChatGPT, Claude, Gemini) undergo a rigorous 3-stage developmental pipeline:

| Pipeline Stage | Training Data | Core Objective | Resulting Model State |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **1. Unsupervised Pre-training** | Trillions of web tokens (Common Crawl, GitHub, books) | Next-token prediction: $\arg\max \sum \ln P(w_t \mid w_{<t})$ | **Base Foundation Model** (raw document completer; cannot converse politely) |
| **2. Supervised Fine-Tuning (SFT)** | Thousands of curated high-quality Q&A dialogues | Teach instruction-following conversational structure | **Instruct Model** (follows prompts, but may be toxic or misaligned) |
| **3. Preference Alignment (RLHF / DPO)**| Pairs of model responses ranked by human annotators | Optimize reward model / direct preference optimization | **Aligned Assistant** (helpful, harmless, and calibrated) |

quizData.question: If you prompt a raw pre-trained Base Model (without SFT or RLHF) with 'Write a poem about the sea', what is it most likely to do?

options.text: Politely say 'Sure, here is your poem!'
Continue the prompt with more bullet points or quiz questions like 'Write a poem about the sun'
Throw a Python runtime syntax exception
Refuse to generate text due to alignment safety rules

quizData.explanation: Base models are text completers; they frequently treat instructions as homework assignment lists and predict subsequent questions rather than executing the instruction.

slides.title: Scaling Laws & Chinchilla Optimality 📈
slides.content:
# Compute, Parameters, and Data

In 2022, DeepMind published the **Chinchilla Scaling Laws** (Hoffmann et al.), disproving the notion that models should simply be made larger:

* For compute-optimal training, model parameter count and training token count should scale in **equal proportion** (~20 tokens per model parameter).
* A 7-billion parameter model trained on 2 trillion tokens (like LLaMA) dramatically outperforms a 70-billion parameter model trained on only 300 billion tokens, while running 10x faster during inference!

slides.title: AI Pro Tip: Parameter-Efficient Fine-Tuning (LoRA) 💡
slides.content:
## Low-Rank Adaptation (LoRA)
Fine-tuning all 70B parameters of an LLM requires massive GPU clusters. **LoRA (Hu et al., 2021)** freezes the original weights and injects low-rank decomposition matrices ($A \in \mathbb{R}^{d \times r}, B \in \mathbb{R}^{r \times d}$ with $r \ll d$).

This reduces trainable parameters by **99%**, allowing custom LLMs to be fine-tuned on a single consumer GPU!
